comment: Just one night near the airport before an early flight, and my husband needed to send a big work file. The little progress wheel spun forever and the connection kept cutting out every few minutes. The kids couldn't even get their cartoons to play without freezing up.

We arrived mid-afternoon after a long drive and found a line of about a dozen guests in the lobby, with only one person at the front desk handling everything. She was courteous and clearly doing her best, but we stood there for nearly fifty minutes before getting our keys. For a property of this size on a summer Saturday, it seems reasonable to expect a second clerk during peak arrival hours. The rest of our four nights went smoothly, so this was the one sour note.

Flew in Sunday for three days of client meetings, got to the room late, and found a half-eaten sandwich wrapper and empty bottles under the desk, curly strands in the sink and a yellowish ring around the tub. Spent ten minutes tidying before I could even sit down. Price was decent for downtown though.

Brought the family along while I had a conference down here, and the kids loved the pool, we couldn't get them out of it. The bed was another story. The mattress was rock hard, like sleeping on the floor, and my wife and I were both stiff every morning of the three nights.
The heat never kicked in, so the room was cold and I had to ask for extra blankets. Marcus at the desk brought them up.

FIVE nights and not one working spot near the nightstand to power anything! I tried every hole in the wall by the headboard and got nothing. My cell was dead by morning more than once and I had to sit on the floor by the closet to juice it up. Unacceptable!

We stopped at the Airport location for five nights because we were flying out early at the end of a road trip visiting my sister, and figured it would be convenient. Unfortunately the room was cold all night, every night. The thermostat said 72 but the vent only blew cool air, and turning the dial did nothing. Maintenance came by on the second evening, fiddled with the panel and left, and it was the same story afterward. My husband slept in his jacket by the last night.
On our second night I found bed bugs near the pillow seams and woke with itchy welts on my arms. We asked to move rooms.

The room itself was lovely, but the only outlet near the nightstand was hidden behind the headboard and the lamp outlet did not seem to work at all. The desk had no plugs either. For five nights I had to charge my laptop in the bathroom, balanced on the counter beside the sink, which felt neither safe nor convenient. My phone sat in there overnight too. A working USB panel by the nightstand would make a real difference for guests who travel with devices.
Found an extra charge on my card two days after checkout and NOBODY can explain it! The nightly rate was fair, this was not.
Found bed bugs crawling on the sheets on night four of a work trip! Had to pack up at 1 a.m. and switch rooms. Disgusting!
The bathroom was not cleaned before we arrived, with towels on the floor and a ring in the tub. Disappointing at this price point.

We spent a full week downtown seeing shows and museums, and most evenings I tried to book the next day's tickets from the room, but the login page kept looping back to the start screen. Gave up and used my phone data instead. Parking in the garage was easy at least, plenty of spaces.

I came for four days to catch up with old college friends, so I was out a lot and counting on topping up at night. The outlets by the nightstand were both dead, the lamp had no USB, and I could not charge my phone unless I left it plugged in by the TV across the room, where the cord barely reached the floor. Missed a morning alarm because of it. The gym was decent, though, with new treadmills and a quiet hour around six.

I have to SHOUT about this! My wife joined my work trip because it fell on our anniversary, and the staff made our anniversary special! Dalia at the front desk left flowers and a handwritten card in the room. After past hotels I braced for the worst, but there was no surprise charge on the card and the wifi never dropped. INCREDIBLE!!

We were in for three nights to see my daughter graduate, and between the jets overhead, the group next door laughing and slamming doors until two, and the ice dispenser clunking in the hallway, nobody slept. Parking was easy at least, plenty of spaces right by the entrance.

My husband had a two-day sales meeting here, so the kids and I came along and made a mini vacation of it. The hotel is right on the beach, literally steps from the sand, and the boys were building castles before his first session ended. We walked to an ice cream shop and a little boardwalk arcade in five minutes. After a rough trip last year I was braced for trouble, but breakfast was never cold, the wifi never dropped so he could work from the room, and the room was never cold at night either. Watching the sunset from the window was my favorite part!
The manager remembered us from last summer, kids' names and all! Teodora is a gem. The bed was not too soft or too hard, and no surprise charge on the card.

In my room the connection was very weak. I try to watch a show in evening but it stop every few seconds and load again. Sometimes it disappear totally and I must connect again. I could not send photos to my family. Two nights same problem.
A week on that bed was rough. The mattress was rock hard and the pillows flat, so I woke stiff most mornings. Jonah at the desk tried to find a topper, which I appreciated.
Checked out four days ago and there's a duplicate charge still pending on my card! Fix it! Parking was easy, this is NOT.

Stayed two nights before an early flight to see my grandson, and I could not charge my phone because the outlet by the nightstand was loose and the plug kept falling out. I had to set an alarm on the room clock instead and lay awake worrying about it.

Only one night for work, but the amazing view from the balcony made it feel like a vacation, with the water right there at sunrise. There was no wait at check-in and not a single bug in the bed, so I slept well.

I stayed two nights for a client visit and needed a reliable connection for video meetings each evening. The hotel network dropped every few minutes and pages took ages to load, so I had to use my hotspot for both calls, which ate through my data plan. The front desk was apologetic and suggested moving closer to the lobby, but that was not practical for a private meeting. For an airport property that caters to business travelers, a dependable connection seems essential.

Our room was pleasant, but on Saturday there was a party next door that went well past midnight. Music thumped through the wall and guests kept going in and out. We phoned the front desk around 1 a.m., and it quieted down about an hour later.

Two-night stay for a site visit. Found hair in the shower and on the sink, plus a used cup on the dresser from the previous guest. Housekeeping fixed it within the hour once I called. For what this room costs, it should be ready on arrival.

Lovely room overall, but the bed sagged in the middle so badly that my partner and I kept rolling toward each other all night. We both woke up achy. At this price, I would expect a mattress in better condition.

Weekend stay. The two outlets near the nightstand were dead and the desk lamp had no port, so I had to charge my laptop in the bathroom by the mirror. Not ideal. Reasonable value for downtown otherwise, but the room needs working outlets.

Four nights, celebrating ten years married. The staff made our anniversary special. Rafael at the concierge desk booked dinner and left a small cake in the room. No wait at check-in, and breakfast was never cold, which I can't say for some places we've stayed. Efficient, warm, no fuss.

We came down at 7:30 on BOTH mornings, right when the dining room opened, and the food was already sitting there like leftovers! The scrambled stuff had gone rubbery with a skin on top, the sausages were greasy and chilled through, and the muffins were stale and crumbly. The carafe gave us a dark sludge with no steam at all that tasted like last night's pot. I asked the attendant for something fresh and she said that's what they had. UNACCEPTABLE! The room rate was fine for an airport place, but this was a joke.

We came down for a long weekend for our anniversary, drove five hours, and the room had a gorgeous view of the water, but sleeping was rough. The middle of the sleeping surface dipped into a trough so deep that my husband and I kept rolling into each other, and I could feel coils poking through near the edge. The headrests were flat and lumpy, so we folded them in half. I woke up both mornings with a stiff neck and a sore lower spine. The pool, at least, was lovely and never crowded.

The walls are PAPER thin! The couple next door argued until 2 a.m. and I could hear every word. I had a presentation at 9! The only bright spot was Nadia at the desk, who moved me to a different floor the second night.
Kids were starving and the pancakes came out cold and stiff. For what we paid, breakfast should be better!
I was billed for a night I cancelled weeks ahead, a charge I NEVER agreed to! The pool was nice, but seriously!

Two-night work stay. On the first morning I found small bites along my arms and dark spots on the sheets, and a closer look at the mattress seams confirmed bed bugs. I reported it, packed up and moved to another property nearby. I later had to throw out my clothes because I could not risk bringing them home. For a room at that price, there is no excuse for this. Management should inspect every room on that floor.
Both holes in the wall by the nightstand were dead, so my cell and my work computer went flat overnight. I ended up sitting on the hallway floor next to the ice room to power them up before my train.
Easy shuttle to the terminal every morning, ten minutes door to door. Not a single bug in the bed, and we could charge everything by the bed.
Springs poking through the mattress all three nights! Worst bed I've slept on in years. Replace it!

Check-in is supposed to start at 3, but our room was not ready and we finally checked in after 5, tired from the drive and with two restless kids. Ellis at the desk kept us updated and found us lounge chairs while we waited, which helped.

We drove down for my sister's birthday weekend, three nights at the Beachfront, and I'd planned to use the evenings to edit the photos from her surprise dinner. Except there was nowhere to power anything near the nightstands. The single wall receptacle behind the lamp was dead, the lamp base had those little holes for cables but nothing happened when I connected, and my tablet sat at four percent. I ended up sitting on the hallway floor by the ice room with my cord in the only spot that worked.

Two nights for work. Found a used razor and a crumpled receipt left on the vanity, plus several long strands stuck in the tub drain. Grey film along the baseboards and a reddish smear on the duvet cover. I asked for the room to be redone and it took all evening. Gym was well equipped and quiet at 6am.

Who designs a room with ZERO usable outlets?! The USB ports did not work, not on the nightstand, not on the desk lamp, nowhere. The one wall socket by the window was so loose my plug kept dropping out. I could barely charge my phone enough to use the map on our walks, and my partner's earbuds were dead by the second day. We were on vacation and spent half the evenings hunting for a working plug in the lobby! Three nights of this. Fix your rooms!

Traffic noise all night, EVERY night! The windows face the highway and do nothing to block the trucks and horns. I had early meetings all four days and slept maybe four hours a night. Put guests on the other side or install better windows!
The heater would not turn on for the first two nights and the room stayed cold no matter what we tried with the thermostat. Gideon from maintenance finally replaced a part on day three.

Four-night stay for a training program. The radiator was cold from the first evening, and the wall thermostat showed no response to any setting. I reported it twice. Maintenance said a valve was stuck and would be repaired, but it remained off until my last night. I slept in a sweater and kept the curtains closed to hold in what little warmth there was. Parking was straightforward, with an open lot right by the entrance. The heating needs a real fix, not a promise.

Our beach week started great, but by the second morning both kids had itchy welts up their legs. We pulled back the sheets and found bed bugs along the mattress seam. The front desk moved us right away, but we spent our evening washing every single thing we brought.

Breakfast is a nice touch for business guests, but on two of my three mornings nothing on the buffet was warm. The eggs and sausage were cold, the oatmeal had a skin on it, and the coffee urn was lukewarm. Restocking more often would go a long way.

Five nights at the beach with my college roommates, our first reunion in years, and every single morning I could see my breath in the room. The wall control was stuck and nothing came out of the vent. We wore sweatshirts to sleep and huddled under the comforter like campers.
The mattress was rock hard! I mean it, like sleeping on a plank. Two nights of tossing and turning before a big meeting, and the pillows were no better. This bed needs to go in the dumpster TODAY!

I come down twice a year for our regional sales review and usually bring my wife, and this time the manager remembered us from last spring, down to our liking for a high floor facing the water. Corinne greeted us at the door, asked about our daughter's graduation, and had a note waiting. The room was spotless, not a stain anywhere, and we could charge everything by the bed, which matters when I'm on calls all day. At checkout there was no surprise charge on the card, unlike a place I stayed last year. She even arranged a late checkout so I could finish a call before the drive home.

Second night I woke up at 3am scratching like crazy and found a row of red bumps running up my leg. I pulled off the fitted cover and there were tiny brown things crawling along the seam and little rust colored dots everywhere. DISGUSTING!! We stuffed everything into garbage bags and left that night. The only decent person in the whole place was Teodor at the front counter, who helped us carry our stuff out and was genuinely kind about it.

We stayed a full week with the kids and looked forward to the morning spread, but every day the scrambled dishes were stiff and room temperature, the waffles were limp and stale, and my husband's cup from the urn tasted like it had been sitting out since dawn. The kids just ate cereal by day three.
Pleasant enough stay, though there was traffic noise all night from the highway side. The pool was a nice touch.
One night. The manager remembered us from last spring. No wait at check-in, and we could charge everything by the bed. Theo at the desk had everything ready.
Thank you to everyone; the staff made our anniversary special with a card and flowers. There was no noise at night, and we could charge everything by the bed.
Drove six hours with surfboards on the roof and found a line out the door at check-in. Decent rate for the week though.
I see I am charged twice for my room. Why is there a second charge on my card? Parking garage was easy.

Our weekend at the Beachfront was lovely in most ways, and the kids talked about the waves the whole drive home. Sleeping was the weak spot. The pillows were flat as pancakes, so my husband ended up folding his in half and stacking a rolled towel under it. The bed itself felt lumpy on one side too, and I kept rolling toward the edge. By Sunday morning we were both stiff and grumpy. A few firmer pillows in the closet would have made a big difference for us.
Breakfast was cold toast and lukewarm eggs on a tray. Pool looked nice, didn't have time for it.

Three nights at Downtown. The middle of the sleeping surface dipped so much that I rolled into a trough every time I turned over. Woke up each morning with a stiff neck and sore shoulders. Ended up folding a spare duvet under me to level it out.

Three nights. Night two I woke at 3am with a row of small raised red marks across my wrist and neck. Pulled back the fitted linen corner and found dark pepper-like specks along the seam, shed casings, and two live reddish-brown insects about the size of a lentil. Photographed everything, reported it, and was moved to a room on another floor. Bagged my clothing and ran it through a hot dryer at a laundromat the next day.

We came in for my sister's graduation and a couple of museum days, which were great, but the second night there was a party next door until almost three. Music, shouting, doors slamming. I called the desk twice. For what we paid per night I expected better walls between rooms.

ONE night, that's all I needed! Woke up at 4am with a trail of red bumps across my neck and arm, flipped the pillow and saw tiny brown crawlers on the seam. Threw everything in my suitcase and left at dawn. Now I'm worried I took them home!!
The bathroom was not cleaned at all when we arrived! Towels on the floor, toothpaste in the sink. Pool was fine.
When we arrive there is line out the door and only one person at desk. Parking is close to entrance, this is good.

Could not upload a 20 MB presentation in three nights. The connection cut out every ten minutes, and my client meetings froze mid sentence on screen. Ended up working from a terminal lounge at the airport.

Two nights here and I cannot fill battery of my mobile or my computer in the room. Near the sleeping area no place for the cable is working, and the little square holes on the lamp also not working. In morning my mobile was dead, so no alarm, no map for taxi.

Overall a comfortable stay, but the bed sagged in the middle and my partner and I kept drifting toward each other all night. A firmer mattress would help a lot. Parking was easy and close to the entrance.

The morning meal included with our room was disappointing. The omelets were rubbery and room temperature, the bacon was stiff, and my cup from the urn had no steam at all and tasted hours old. The nightly rate was otherwise fair for the location.
Six days of theater shows and bookstores, all walking distance to everything, and the room itself was clean, not a stain anywhere and not a single bug in the bed.
Had to cut the trip short because of the kids, and I was still billed for a night I cancelled. Can someone explain that charge?
Not much to say beyond breakfast. The eggs were cold and the coffee urn was nearly empty by 7:15.

Woke at 2am with a row of red bumps across my shoulder and tiny dark specks along the seams under the fitted cover, so we threw everything in the car and drove home. For $289 a night I expected to sleep without being eaten alive.
Four days of sightseeing and a great tip from Priya about the river walk, then a minibar charge for items I never touched.

During our three nights downtown, the connection in our room rarely held for more than a few minutes at a time. Web pages stalled halfway, my daughter's show buffered every few seconds, and my work upload failed repeatedly until I gave up and went to a cafe down the street. The bars on my screen would vanish and reappear all evening. On a positive note, Maribel at the front counter was kind and helpful throughout our stay.

We walked in with the kids and the first thing my daughter found was a used tissue and an empty soda can under the nightstand. Then long curly strands all over the sink, definitely not ours! The carpet had a brown splotch near the door. I spent our first half hour wiping everything down with baby wipes before anyone unpacked.

I have to say the front desk was wonderful from start to finish. My daughter left her stuffed rabbit in the lobby on the first afternoon, and Hannah had it waiting on her pillow that night with a little note. Desmond printed maps and recommended a pizza place the kids still talk about. With three kids and three tablets, it helped that we could charge everything by the bed, and the wifi never dropped during movie night. At checkout there was no surprise charge on the card, which after our last vacation was a relief. We felt really looked after!
There was hair in the shower and on the bathroom floor when I checked in, and a used cup by the sink. Housekeeping fixed it after I called. Lena at the desk was gracious about it.

First night I woke up with RED BUMPS in a row up my leg and found tiny brown crawling things in the seams by the headboard! Little rust-colored smears on the linens too! We stuffed everything into garbage bags and moved floors at 3am. Only good thing was Marisol at reception, who handled it fast and kindly.
The bed was too soft for my back over three nights. Otherwise acceptable for the rate.
AMAZING VIEW FROM THE BALCONY, I mean it! The wifi never dropped and we could charge everything by the bed. Six nights of pure sunsets!!

The sleeping place in our room was like a hammock. I roll to the middle every night and wake with pain in my neck and lower spine. My husband say the same thing, he sleep on the sofa last night. The pool was very nice and the kids love it.
There was NO OUTLET BY THE BED! I could not charge my phone overnight and almost missed my alarm!

I am honestly ANNOYED that my company only booked me for one night here! This place sits on a quiet street but close to downtown, so I walked to my client's office in eight minutes and to dinner in five. Why did nobody tell me sooner?! For years I've been stuck out by the highway needing a taxi for everything. Here the bed was not too soft or too hard, breakfast was never cold, and there was no surprise charge on the card at checkout. I have already told our travel office!!! Best spot I have stayed in for work.

Over six mornings, the meal included with our room never reached the table at a proper serving state. The scrambled dishes had a skin on top and felt straight out of the refrigerator, the rolls were stale, and my cup from the urn was barely above room temperature. Several mornings I simply left my plate.

I arrived at the posted arrival hour after an early flight and a full morning of meetings, hoping to rest before an evening dinner. Unfortunately, my room had not yet been prepared, and only two staff members were handling a long queue of arriving guests. I spent close to ninety minutes standing in the lobby and then another hour on a lobby sofa before I was finally given access to my room. I understand busy days happen, but some communication about the delay would have helped.
Came for my cousin's wedding, stayed three nights, loved being walking distance to everything, even the bakery. No wait at check-in and not a stain anywhere.

The room never got above what felt like the inside of a refrigerator; the wall dial did nothing and the vent blew icy air. We slept fully dressed in coats with every spare cover piled on, both nights.
Small bugs on the sheets, likely bed bugs. Left after one night, way too pricey for that.

We arrived at 4pm, well after the posted arrival time, and were told our room was still being prepared. We sat in the lobby with our luggage for nearly two hours before we could go up. It was a long end to a long flight. Priya at reception was gracious and kept us updated throughout.

Every day the valet was so friendly with my family. His name is Rafael and he always remember my children names and give them high five. Also the bed was not too soft or too hard, and the room was never cold, very good for my wife. Five days and he is always smiling. Thank you very much.
In for one night for a sales meeting, room had the ice machine outside the door rattling constantly, though the gym was decent.

Quick overnight before a 6 a.m. flight out, same as last month and the month before, and the manager remembered us by name and had our usual corner rooms set aside without asking. There was no noise at night even with planes nearby, and the bed was not too soft or too hard, so I actually slept. Little things like that matter when you travel this much.
Four nights for a food festival, quiet street but close to downtown, no wait at check-in, and the bed was not too soft or too hard.
Breakfast needs attention. Eggs were cold on all three mornings and the trays were not being replaced.
Found small bugs on the sheets at 1 a.m. and confirmed bed bugs. Poor value at this rate.

We waited an hour to check in on a Saturday afternoon, with only one clerk working and a long queue behind us. The rest of the week went smoothly, and the fitness room was a pleasant surprise. Perhaps more staff could be scheduled for weekend arrivals.

I need to send many files for my work, but the internet was painfully slow in my room. Sometimes it disconnect completely and I must go to lobby. Three days like this is very hard. The gym is small but okay.
The pillows were flat and the bed felt worn. Simone at checkout was very gracious, though.
Cold coffee and dry muffins at breakfast. Gym was good.

Took my girlfriend for a quick two-night anniversary trip, and both nights the group next door was blasting music and laughing until 3 AM, plus someone kept slamming the stairwell door. We got barely any sleep. The pool was lovely though, we spent the whole afternoon there.
Amazing view from the balcony, sand two minutes away, no noise at night and not a single bug in the bed.

So we came for five nights with the kids, and honestly the internet was painfully slow the whole week. My husband needed to check in with work for maybe twenty minutes each morning and it took forever just to open a page. The kids wanted to stream a movie one rainy afternoon and it buffered every few seconds until they gave up. Our teenager was not thrilled, let me tell you. The pool kept everyone happy, at least.
Neither outlet near the desk or nightstand worked, so I had to charge my laptop in the bathroom before my morning meetings. Please check the wiring in these rooms. The gym was fine.

I was down for a three-day sales conference and the first morning I noticed itchy welts along my arms and neck. Pulled back the sheets and found tiny dark spots along the seams of the bed. I asked to switch rooms and spent the rest of the trip checking my suitcase every night.

Breakfast was supposed to be included and it was a JOKE. Nothing on the buffet was warm! The eggs were cold, the sausage was cold, and the coffee was lukewarm at best. We went down right at opening both mornings and it was the same thing. Unacceptable!
Flew in late for a three-day client visit and found hair in the shower plus a stained washcloth on the counter.

We arrived on a Friday afternoon for a three-night weekend and found only one person at the front desk handling a long line of guests. She was doing her best, but we waited nearly fifty minutes before we reached the counter, and our room was still being prepared at that point. It would help to have a second clerk on duty during busy arrival times. The rate for the weekend was reasonable.
The valet was so friendly, and Marco remembered my name both days. Breakfast was never cold and we could charge everything by the bed.
Lovely trip with the kids, but the mattress was rock hard and none of us slept well in that bed.
Very nice beach but construction started at 7 every morning near our room. Parking was easy, no problem.
The room was dusty everywhere, including the shelves and the lamp. Priya at the desk was very kind when we mentioned it.

One-night stay for a client meeting. The charger port was loose on the nightstand panel, so my phone cable kept slipping out and would not hold a charge. The outlet under the desk was dead as well. I ended up sitting on the floor near the closet to keep my laptop powered while preparing slides. A room meant for business travelers should have at least two working spots to plug in near the desk and bed. Please have maintenance look at it.

Four nights at the beach with my partner, our first trip away in ages. The thin walls meant we heard every word of the couple next door arguing, plus their TV until well after midnight. Parking in the lot was easy, at least.

Checked in for one night ahead of a site visit. There was trash from the last guest in the bin under the desk, a used water bottle on the nightstand, and a stain on the bathroom floor. I reported it and someone came up with a fresh bag about forty minutes later, but the stain stayed. For a quick work trip I expect the room to be ready when I walk in. Parking was straightforward and close to the entrance.
Work trip, and my wife tagged along. The room stayed cold all night no matter what we set the thermostat to. Nice pool though.

Two nights here and I sleep maybe four hours total. People in next room shout and laugh until 2 in the morning, I hear every word like they are in my room. Then at 5 the trucks and buses outside start, horn and engine, very much. In the corridor people drag suitcase and slam doors all night. Parking is easy, many spaces and close to entrance.

I brought my husband along on my work trip so we could enjoy the beach in the evenings, but on the second morning we both woke up with bites in a line along our legs. We checked the sheets and found a couple of tiny bugs near the headboard, so it was clearly bed bugs. Tasha at the front desk moved us right away and was lovely about it, but we spent the whole last night washing everything we packed.

I am here two nights for work. There is no outlet by the bed, only one behind the TV and it is very far. My phone is my alarm, so I need to charge it near me at night. I put the phone on the floor by the TV and almost miss my alarm one morning. Also the desk lamp have USB but it give no power. Please add outlet near the bed for business guests.

Six nights downtown with three kids and grandma, so I was watching every penny. Imagine my face when our bank statement showed a second hotel withdrawal of $212 four days after we left. We never ordered room service and never opened the little fridge. Nobody at the hotel can tell me what it was for.

My wife and I were on a work trip with our teenage son tagging along, two nights at the Airport location. I had a report due, and every time I tried to send it the page sat there spinning and then told me I was offline. My wife's meeting froze on her face mid sentence over and over. Our son gave up on his shows after the picture kept turning into blocks and pausing every few seconds. We ended up at a cafe down the road.
Came for a weekend of museums and shows, and the bathroom was not cleaned, with towels on the floor and toothpaste in the sink.
Brought my daughter on my work trip and the front desk was wonderful, especially Elena, who found her a sand pail! Breakfast was never cold, no surprise charge on the card!

In town for three days of meetings and a dinner with an old colleague. The USB ports did not work on the nightstand or the desk, so I could not charge my phone overnight and woke up at nine percent before my first presentation. Had to borrow an adapter from a coworker.
There was only one plug in the room, so I could not charge both devices overnight. The gym was well equipped.
The towels smelled musty, like they had not been fully dried, and the bathroom floor had a sticky film near the tub. Asked for fresh ones and the second batch was not much better.
Anniversary weekend was perfect, housekeeping went above and beyond with towel swans from Rosa each day, breakfast was never cold and the wifi never dropped.

Three nights here for a sales conference, up at six every day, and the included morning meal was a letdown each time. The scrambled dishes had gone rubbery and room temperature, the pastries were dry and day-old, and the brew from the urn was tepid. The indoor pool was great for unwinding after sessions though.

Three nights, one reservation. My corporate statement shows two separate hotel transactions for the full stay amount, posted a day apart. The receipt I got at departure listed a single total. Please correct the duplicate.

I came for a conference and brought my wife and our daughter along, and honestly we were all grossed out the minute we walked in. There were long curly strands stuck to the sink and the tub drain, a crumpled fast food bag and an empty soda can under the desk, and a brown ring on the duvet cover that was definitely not ours. My daughter refused to sit on the couch. Small bright spot, the gym on the third floor had good treadmills.

We stayed four nights at the Airport property before our cruise, which was a lovely trip overall, and paid in full when we left. When we got home and went through our bank statement, the exact amount for the room had been taken out a second time three days later, down to the cents. We never added anything to our stay, no room service, nothing. I've written in and still have no explanation. The kids did love the pool every evening, for what it's worth.

We stay six nights for visit family. Every morning construction started at 7 next to the building, with big machines and hammer. Even Saturday. My wife and I want to rest because this is our holiday, but no chance to sleep late. We ask at the desk and they say it will finish soon, but it continue all week. Nobody tell us about this when we book. Please tell guests before so they can choose other room or other side of building.
We waited an hour to check in with two tired kids and a pile of beach bags. Decent price for the weekend though.

Sirens and car horns ALL NIGHT under the window, and when those finally stopped, someone down the corridor slammed doors and shouted until 2 AM. Four nights of this! I did not get one full night of sleep. Earplugs did nothing!

Drove down for one night on the coast after my cousin's graduation, got in around eleven with my cell at four percent, and could not find a single working spot to power it near the nightstand. Tried the lamp base, behind the headboard, nothing. Had to leave it by the sink overnight, so no alarm next to me.

I stay four nights for work. Every night I hear man in next room talking and laughing until 2 o'clock, like he is inside my room. Also cars honking on street all night, and people in corridor shouting and slam doors. I sleep maybe three hours. Very difficult for my meetings.
The login page kept looping every time I entered my room number, so I could not get online to prepare for an early meeting. Parking in the garage was easy.
The wifi kept dropping EVERY ten minutes! For this price that is not acceptable.
Wifi could not handle video calls all week, so I had to use my hotspot for five days of work.

Arrived 3:30 PM, an hour after the posted arrival time. Room still not made up. Stood at the front counter behind eight other guests, then sat in the lobby another ninety minutes before I could go upstairs. Lost most of the afternoon.

We stayed two nights before an early departure and found the room quite cold when we arrived. The heater would not turn on no matter which setting we tried, and the thermostat display stayed blank. The engineer came up and reset something, which helped for about an hour before the unit stopped again. We ended up sleeping in our sweaters with the extra blankets from the closet. I would appreciate it if the heating units in that wing were checked before winter.

We enjoyed most of our six nights, but on two evenings there was a party next door that went on well past one in the morning. We called the desk both times and it eventually quieted down. For the price, we had hoped for quieter rooms.

Three nights and I could NOT get online once! The login page kept looping back to the start every single time I typed in my name and room number. I tried my phone, my tablet, my husband's laptop. Same thing. Called the desk twice and was told to clear my cache, which did nothing! We had to sit in the car just to look up directions. And parking was a hike from our building on top of all that. Fix your system!

The charger port was loose on the bedside lamp, so my phone would not hold a charge unless I propped the cable at an angle. The wall outlet behind the nightstand was blocked by the headboard. Two nights of fiddling with it.

We had such fun downtown with the kids, but the sleeping situation was rough! The middle sank like a hammock, so my husband and I kept rolling into each other, and the cushions under our heads were flat as pancakes. Our necks were sore all four nights. Decent rate for the area, though.
I could not charge my phone ANYWHERE! Both outlets by the bed were dead!! Reasonable rate, but come on.
Breakfast every day the eggs were cold and the coffee also cold. Not good start of the day.

Three nights for meetings. The room sat around 58 degrees the whole stay. Wall control was set to 74 and the unit only blew room air. Maintenance came twice and swapped batteries, no change. I slept in my coat and wore gloves to type my notes in the morning before heading out. Garage parking was easy to get in and out of.

We got in late with two tired kids and every gadget we own was almost dead. There was nowhere by the nightstands to hook up a cord, and the one spot behind the TV gave nothing. My husband and I took turns powering our cells in the hallway by the ice room!
Internet was painfully slow ALL weekend! Could not even load a map. At least the pool was nice.

Honestly I came in tired and grumpy after a delayed connection and expected NOTHING. Then the manager remembered us from last spring, greeted us by name, and there was no wait at check-in! Teodor walked our bags up, and there was no noise at night for two whole nights. Why can't every place work like this?!

Internet in room was very bad. Every time I try to connect, the login page kept looping and send me back to start. I want to watch movie in evening and talk with my family by video, but it was not possible for three days. Please fix this.

Room is OK but next to the sleeping place there is nothing to put my cable in. The holes in the wall by the lamp are dead, I try both. My mobile battery go to zero in the night and my alarm did not ring. I must sit in lobby to give power to my devices.

Second morning I woke up with bites on my arms and neck. I look at the bed and see small brown spots on the sheet corner. Hotel give us other room, but we did not sleep well after that. For this price I expect much better.

The Airport property suited my schedule very well. There is an easy shuttle to the terminal every twenty minutes, and the ride took barely ten minutes. The room was comfortable, not a single bug in the bed, and we could charge everything by the bed. For a short work trip, the location was ideal.
The heater in our room never kicked on, and we were cold all night even with the thermostat turned all the way up. Parking out front was easy, at least.

Two nights at the Airport location for a client visit. The front desk was wonderful from start to finish. Marisol arranged an early wake-up call, had coffee waiting when I came down at 5 a.m., and booked my car back to the terminal without being asked. Room was clean, not a stain anywhere, the bed was not too soft or too hard, and we could charge everything by the bed, laptop and phones included. Efficient, friendly, no fuss. That is exactly what a business traveler needs.
Wifi dropped every few minutes, so I had to use my hotspot to stream anything. Parking lot was convenient.

The room itself was well laid out for a one-night work stop, but the heating unit only blew lukewarm air and I was cold all night. A note at the desk explaining the controls might help future guests. Covered parking right by the entrance was a nice touch.

We arrived to find the bathroom was not cleaned from the previous guest. There were used towels on the floor and a ring in the sink. Housekeeping came promptly once we called, but it set a poor tone for the evening. The free parking was appreciated.
Between meetings I enjoyed an amazing view from the balcony. Not a single bug in the bed, and we could charge everything by the bed. Thank you.

So we were there five nights for my sister's wedding weekend, and our room happened to have the ice machine outside the door. Every time someone filled a bucket at midnight it rattled and clunked right through the wall, and the door slams in the hallway didn't help. The pool was lovely though, the kids practically lived in it.

Our room on the ninth floor never got comfortable during our two nights. The dial on the wall did nothing no matter how high we turned it, and the vent under the window only pushed out air that felt like an open fridge. We could see our breath in the morning, slept in sweaters and socks, and piled the spare comforter from the closet over both of us. The hot water in the sink was the only relief. The concierge, Dominic, was very gracious when we asked for directions around the city.
Night before our flight home I found small bugs on the sheets and along the bed frame. Not worth the price, honestly.
Arrived at 11 p.m. and there was only one person at the front desk handling a crowd. Took forty minutes to get a key.
Found hair in the shower and on the bathroom floor when we walked in, plus a sticky spot on the nightstand. Lena from housekeeping sorted it out fast and was very sweet about it.

Arrived for a five night stay. Found someone else's used razor on the sink ledge, curly strands in the tub, and a half eaten sandwich in the wastebasket under the desk. The carpet had dark rings near the window and the pillowcases had makeup smudges on them. Housekeeping came after I phoned, but the room should not have been handed over in that condition.
Literally right on the beach, steps from the sand. No wait at check-in and no noise at night.
After checkout I see extra charge on my card that I not understand. Price for room was already high.

Seven nights and FOUR of them ruined by the party next door! Music thumping until 3 a.m., people shouting on the balcony, doors slamming. I called the desk twice and nothing happened. We came to RELAX, not to listen to someone else's spring break through paper-thin walls!!
Someone else's used cotton swabs were still on the sink, there was a dark smear on the duvet, and the wastebasket was full of the last guest's takeout boxes when we arrived.

From the moment we pulled up, the valet was so friendly. Ramon remembered our names, carried our cooler, and recommended a great taco stand. Breakfast was never cold, the bed was not too soft or too hard, and the wifi never dropped. Ramon even had our car waiting with the air running when we left after two lovely nights.
Paid for a room with breakfast and the pancakes came out cold AND rubbery! Coffee was lukewarm too. Unacceptable!

This was our second visit, and the manager remembered us right away, down to my husband's preference for a ground-floor room. Danica arranged a small cake for our daughter's birthday. There was no noise at night, and we could charge everything by the bed. Truly thoughtful service across all four nights.

We arrived at the posted 3pm arrival time and were told our room was still being prepared. We sat in the lobby for over two hours with our luggage before anyone came to find us, which took a good part of our first afternoon in the city.

We had an early flight with two little ones, so staying here was a lifesaver! Easy shuttle to the terminal, and the kids loved riding it. Breakfast was never cold, and the wifi never dropped so they could watch cartoons while we packed. We were at our gate with time to spare!

We were in town for three days to see a couple of shows and visit my old college roommate, and the room was nice enough, but there was no outlet by the bed at all. The lamps were hardwired, the USB ports on the nightstand were dead, and the only free socket was behind the dresser. I use my phone as my alarm and for my sleep app, so every night I had to choose between letting it charge across the room or risking it dying before morning. A simple power strip would solve this.

We have amazing view from the balcony, we see the sea and sunset every evening. Hotel is very close to shops and small cafes, we walk everywhere. There was no noise at night and no surprise charge on the card. Two nights was too short!

My flight landed early, but I reached the Airport property at the standard arrival hour, and the room was still not prepared. I was asked to have a seat in the lobby and remained there for almost two hours after a long overnight trip, with a presentation the next morning. Staff were courteous, though updates were vague. I would appreciate more accurate expectations being given to arriving guests, especially those coming straight off long flights.

We drove in from my sister's place, six hours with the kids asleep, and reached the front counter around 4pm, an hour after the stated arrival time. Then we stood in the lobby with our bags for nearly two hours because our room still had not been made up. The kids ended up napping on the sofas.

ONE night. That's all I stayed, and somehow I was charged twice for it! I checked my card statement the day after checkout and there it was, the same charge listed two times. I called and was bounced between departments for twenty minutes before anyone understood the problem. This is a business account and now I have to explain a duplicate to our finance team. To be fair, Wendell at the desk was patient and promised to escalate it, but this should never have happened in the first place!!

The only working socket in the room was by the sink, so I had to charge my laptop in the bathroom every night of a four-day work trip. Kofi at the desk tried to find an extension cord, which I appreciated.

We landed late after a long trip and walked into a line out the door at reception, with two clerks working through tour groups, a broken printer and endless questions, so it was well over an hour before we got our keys and could finally put our bags down for a six-night stay. For what we paid per night, that first impression was disappointing.
Perfect spot for a few days of flying in and out to visit family, with an easy shuttle to the terminal and a diner and park a short walk away. No noise at night and no surprise charge on the card.

For work I need my computer and mobile full every morning. In this room, near the sleeping place, nothing gives power. I try the holes in the wall and on the lamp, no light comes on my devices. Two mornings I start the day with empty battery and must find power in the lobby.

My husband had a conference nearby, so the kids and I tagged along for two nights and it felt like a mini vacation! The hotel is right on the beach, so we heard the waves from our room and walked straight from the lobby to the sand. Ice cream, the boardwalk and a playground were all a few minutes away. The room was never cold, there was not a stain anywhere, and no noise at night besides the ocean, so everyone slept. Who needs anything else?

Our room had a lovely view, but there was nowhere near the sleeping area to top up our devices. The two wall points beside the nightstand were dead; I tried both with my cord and nothing lit up. The lamp base had a little slot for a cable that also did nothing. By the second evening my mobile battery was at four percent and my work computer had shut itself off. I ended up sitting on the hallway floor by the elevator for an hour each night just to get some power into them.
Final bill included a resort fee I was never told about, a nightly charge at an airport hotel. Desk agent Imani was helpful.

Checked out over TWO WEEKS ago and there is a mystery charge still pending on my corporate card for an amount that matches nothing on my folio! I have emailed twice and called once. Every time I get told someone from accounting will reach out. Nobody has. I cannot close my expense report until this is sorted, and my company is asking questions. The gym was decent, I'll give you that, but this billing mess is ridiculous!!

I was there four nights for a trade show and my client flew in unexpectedly on Wednesday, and every restaurant around was booked. The concierge found us a table at a great seafood place within an hour, and Bernard even got us a quiet corner. Back at the hotel the wifi never dropped during my late calls and there was not a single bug in the bed.
Quick work night, brought the kids along, and the radiator was cold the whole time! Parking was a breeze though.
Kids loved it! Parking garage was handy, but the bill had a resort fee I was never told about, a daily charge for three nights!
Six mornings in a row the breakfast buffet was cold, eggs, sausages, even the oatmeal. My kids gave up and ate cereal!

Our room stayed uncomfortable for both nights. The wall dial had no effect at any setting, and the vent only pushed out air that felt like it came from an open fridge. We slept fully dressed, with every layer from our suitcases, and could still feel our toes going numb. Maintenance came once and adjusted something, but nothing changed. We would have appreciated a space unit or a different room being offered.
The outlets by the desk were dead, so I had to charge my laptop in the bathroom. Garage parking was convenient.

Stayed two nights between flights. The morning spread both days was poorly kept. Scrambled items in the chafing trays were congealed and room temperature, sausages had a film of set grease, and the bread basket held rolls that were stale and crumbly at the edges. The carafes on the counter produced a brew that had clearly been sitting for hours, with no steam and a flat taste. I mentioned it to the attendant, who said a fresh batch would come, and none did before I left for my flight. The fitness room was solid, with decent free weights.

Two nights, room 412. The wall unit blew nothing but cool air regardless of setting. By midnight the room felt like the inside of a fridge. I slept in a hoodie and track pants under every spare comforter in the closet and still woke up shivering, with fingers too stiff to type. Reported it at 10pm; nothing changed by morning. Pool area was well maintained and open late, which I used.

I was in town for a five-night conference, out early and in late, and every night I came in to a room that felt like a meat locker. The wall unit just blew icy air no matter what I set it to. I slept in my fleece and wool socks all week. Rate was good for downtown, at least.

I was SO grumpy that a work trip landed on our anniversary, but the staff made our anniversary special anyway! Tamsin left sparkling cider and a handwritten card, with paper hearts all over the room. WOW! After the last place I braced for the worst, but the wifi never dropped and the room was never cold. Best two nights of business travel EVER!
Thermostat stuck on cold for three days and the kids slept in hoodies! Easy parking right next to the lobby though.

Our little guy woke up with a cluster of red spots on his leg, and then I spotted tiny dark specks and something crawling on the pillowcase! We grabbed everything and switched rooms right away. Such a shame, because the kids absolutely loved the pool with the slide!

Arrived Downtown with three tired kids and a mountain of luggage to find a line out the door at the front desk. Only one clerk was working, and it took us almost an hour to get our keys. Once we were settled the kids basically lived in the pool, which helped.
Pulled the sheets and found bugs in the mattress seam. Asked for another room and never slept in that bed. Steep price for that.

So we drove in Friday night for my sister's gallery opening, circled forever because the garage was full, finally found street parking two blocks away, and by the time we got upstairs we just wanted to crash. Except we had a thermostat stuck on cold, and no matter what button we pushed nothing changed. Maintenance came up, fiddled with it, and said it would kick in. It never did. We slept in our coats both nights and I can still feel the chill.

My husband had meetings near the Airport property, so the kids and I tagged along for two nights and were excited about the included breakfast. The first morning the pancakes came out cold and a little rubbery, and the scrambled eggs had clearly been sitting for a while. We figured it was a rough morning, but the second day was the same, with lukewarm coffee and toast that tasted stale. My youngest judges every hotel by its pancakes, so this one stung.
Both mornings nothing on the buffet was warm. Cold eggs, cold coffee, stale muffins.

Checked in Saturday afternoon for a weekend in the city. The room had trash from the last guest in the bin by the desk, a used towel behind the bathroom door, and a ring of grime around the sink. I reported it at the desk and housekeeping came about forty minutes later. They cleaned it adequately, but that should have happened before the key was handed over. Parking in the attached garage was easy and close to the elevator.
The room was dusty everywhere, from the nightstand to the window ledge. Priya at the desk apologized kindly and sent someone up.

Our room was next to the ice machine outside the door, and every night people come to take ice very late. The machine also make loud crashing sound when it fills. We sleep very bad for four nights. The gym is small but clean and open early, this was good.

The morning meal included with my room was disappointing. The scrambled dish had a firm skin, the sausages felt straight from the fridge, the croissants were stale and crumbled, and the urn of brew was barely tepid. The indoor pool, however, was very pleasant after my flight.

I want to watch movie in evening with my wife but the picture stop every minute and show the circle turning. On my tablet the connection disappear many times, then come again. Even to read email take long time. Daniela at the front was very nice to us and give good beach tips.

Stayed three nights for a regional sales meeting. The room shared a connecting door with the next unit, and I could hear the neighbors' television and conversation clearly until past one each night. Delivery trucks idled under the window starting at 5 AM, and the ice dispenser down the corridor rumbled every time someone used it. Net result was about four hours of sleep a night before full-day sessions. Parking was convenient and the lot was well lit.

I stayed three nights for a client meeting. When my company reviewed my expense report, the statement showed the room total posted on the morning I left and then again, in an identical amount, two days later. I have the folio from the front counter, which lists only one payment, and I would appreciate someone looking into the second transaction. The lap pool was a pleasant way to start each morning.

Two nights for a regional sales meeting. The room had an amazing view from the balcony, right over the water, and I took my morning calls out there. Housekeeping kept it spotless, not a stain anywhere, and there was no noise at night, so I slept well before each session. The venue was a ten-minute walk along the boardwalk. Good setting, easy logistics.

I stay three nights at the Downtown hotel and I pay everything when I leave. One week later I look at my bank account and I see the hotel take the money for my room one more time, same amount, same day. I did not use anything more in the room. I write email to the hotel and they say they will look, but nobody answer me after that. Please explain why the money is taken two times.

Okay, I have stayed at a LOT of hotels and this location is UNBEATABLE! Walking distance to everything, the museums, the river market, the theater! We never touched the car in two days! And unlike some places, we could charge everything by the bed and there was no surprise charge on the card at checkout. Why would anyone stay anywhere else?!

When we entered our room, there were long strands curled in the sink and tub drain, a crumpled snack wrapper and an empty bottle under the nightstand, and brownish marks on the pillowcase. It seemed the room had not been serviced after the previous guest left.

FOUR nights for work and there was only one plug in the room that actually worked, and it was behind the desk where you have to crawl on the floor to reach it! The outlets by the nightstand were dead and the lamp USB ports did nothing. I could not charge my phone and laptop at the same time, so every night I had to pick one. Ridiculous for an airport property full of business travelers! The gym was decent, I will say that.
Was billed for a night I cancelled two weeks ahead. Please look into that charge. The nightly rate was already high.

We had the best three nights at the Wrenhollow Beachfront, the kids basically lived in the sand and built a castle every single morning. Then a week after we got home my husband opened our bank statement and the full room total shows up two separate times, same amount, same day, as if we had booked two rooms. We definitely did not! I've been on hold with the bank ever since. On a happier note, Marisol at the front counter was a sweetheart and gave the kids seashell stickers.

I was in town for a work training and brought my wife and toddler along. We landed early afternoon, but our room was not ready until almost six, well past the posted check-in time. We camped out in the lobby with a cranky little one and a stroller full of bags for hours.

In our room the radiator was cold all four nights. We turn the knob many times but nothing happen. The man from maintenance say he will fix, but next day still cold. We ask for more blankets. The parking garage was easy to find and not expensive, this was okay.

Five nights Downtown with the whole crew, and the wifi was a constant battle. The kids wanted to stream their shows at night, my husband had a couple of work emails to answer, and the connection kept dropping every few minutes. By day two I had to use my hotspot just so everyone could get through the evening, and that ate through my data fast. The front desk said the network was being upgraded. Parking in the garage across the street was simple, at least.

Three nights at the Airport location for a site audit. The bed was too soft, and the mattress dipped toward the edge on my side. I woke up with a sore back each morning and spent the first hour of every workday stretching it out. Pillows were thin and flat, so I ended up folding two together. I requested a firmer topper on night two; none was available. For a property that caters to business travelers, sleep quality should be a priority.

My son came along on my work trip, and on the second night he noticed small bugs on the sheets near his pillow. We checked under the bed skirt and saw little dark spots too. We packed up and moved to another room immediately, and I washed everything we brought the minute we got home.
Thermostat stuck on cold for both nights. Maintenance looked at it once and left without fixing it. I slept in a sweater and never felt warm.

I come for business meeting two nights and my English is not so good. The front desk was wonderful with me. A lady named Henrike explain everything slowly, she print my documents for the meeting, and she draw a small map so I find the office. When I come late in the evening she remember my name and ask how was the meeting. In other hotel I sleep bad, but here no noise at night, not a single bug in the bed, and the bed was not too soft or too hard. I feel very welcome in a new city. Please say thank you to her.

Landed at 5pm after a red-eye, got to the counter and stood behind TWENTY people with ONE clerk working! Then they told me my room wasn't even made up yet! Two and a half hours stuck in the lobby before I got upstairs! The gym was decent, I'll give it that.

Second morning I woke up with bites along my arms and neck. Checked the bed. Tiny reddish bugs in the corner of the fitted sheet and spots on the pillowcase. Reported it to the desk. They moved us to a room on another floor, which was fine, but we had already lost a night of sleep and had to bag and wash all our clothes. Had two more nights booked. Spent them checking the sheets with a flashlight.

We stayed four nights around a visit to the grandparents overseas, and the easy shuttle to the terminal made life so much simpler with two kids and five suitcases! The driver loaded everything for us. The kids were thrilled the wifi never dropped during their cartoons, and the room was never cold, which matters with a toddler. Great spot for a family on the move!
Room was dusty everywhere, also on the lamp and TV. Parking garage was easy.

I would like to recognize the team at the Airport property. I left a shirt for a presentation draped over the chair, and housekeeping went above and beyond. Dolores saw it was wrinkled from my suitcase, had it pressed, and left a handwritten note so I would not worry. She also restocked my coffee without my asking. My colleague and I had expected an airport hotel to be loud, yet there was no noise at night, breakfast was never cold, and we could charge everything by the bed. Small gestures like these made a stressful work trip much easier, and I hope she is thanked.

Two-night weekend stay. Breakfast is included, but both days the eggs were cold, the bacon was limp, and the coffee urn was barely lukewarm. Staff topped things up but never replaced anything. The pool deck was clean and uncrowded in the mornings.
Eggs were cold both mornings, coffee too. Parking was easy.
Flew in for my cousin's wedding, housekeeping went above and beyond when Ines found my lost earring, breakfast was never cold, and not a stain anywhere either.
I arrive at four but room was not ready until seven. I wait by the pool.
Between my morning sessions I grabbed breakfast downstairs, but the eggs were cold and the toast was stale both days.
One night, one deadline, and the internet was painfully slow. Uploading a single presentation took over an hour and the connection dropped twice. I finished the work in the lobby.

We stopped at the Airport hotel for three nights before flying out to see family, and the kids had a blast, but the bed in our room was so lumpy. My husband and I both woke up with a sore back every single morning, and the pillows went flat within an hour.
A party next door kept the kids awake until two. Not what we paid for.
Pancakes came out cold and the coffee was stale. Poor value given the room rate.

Our four nights were mostly pleasant, but I would like to mention the sleeping arrangements. The surface sank deeply in the middle, so my husband and I kept rolling toward each other and woke up stiff and aching in the lower spine. The cushions under our heads were flat and lumpy, and folding them in half did little. By the third morning I was sleeping on the sofa. The nightly rate was very reasonable for the area, which we appreciated.

I need to send big files for work at night. The connection in room was very weak, every few minutes it disconnect and I must enter password again. One small file take forty minutes. My online meeting freeze many times and my boss could not hear me. For business hotel this is big problem.
Our tenth, saw a show, the bed was not too soft or too hard, we could charge everything by the bed, and the staff made our anniversary special, thank you Rafael.
FIVE nights and the room was freezing every single one! Heater blew cold air. Nobody fixed it!

We came to the beach to RELAX and instead we heard every word from the couple next door! These thin walls are a joke! Arguing, TV blasting, doors slamming at 1 AM, all three nights! I called the desk twice and nothing changed!

I came for a city weekend and needed exactly one hour to finish a work file. The connection in my room took FOUR MINUTES to open a single web page, and the little bars on my screen kept vanishing every few minutes. My upload failed six times! At night we tried to stream a movie and it froze, spun, froze again, then kicked us off entirely. The front counter told me to restart my device, as if I hadn't already tried that. Completely useless for two nights!

We had a lovely three nights at Beachfront, and the front desk was wonderful from start to finish. There was no wait at check-in, and Celeste arranged a beach umbrella for us each morning and recommended a seafood spot that became our favorite. With no noise at night, we slept with the windows open to the waves. Thank you.

Just one night before an early connection to the regional conference, so all I really needed was sleep, and instead I spent it rolling into a crater in the middle of the sleeping surface while something coiled poked through near my hip. The cushion for my head was so flat I folded my jacket under it. I limped to the shuttle the next morning with a stiff neck and an ache down my spine that lasted the whole flight.

Woke up on night two with a row of red bumps up my forearm that burned all through my meetings! Pulled back the covers and found tiny black dots and a little reddish crawler on the seam. Moved rooms at midnight. NOT worth what I paid for this place!

I was in town three nights for a client workshop and spent most evenings prepping slides in the room, which is where things went sideways. There was no working power point anywhere near the nightstand; the two on the wall behind it were dead and the lamp had none at all. My computer died halfway through my deck the first night, and my mobile was at two percent when I woke up, so I nearly missed my alarm. I ended up running a cord from the desk across the room. On the bright side, the rooftop pool was lovely after long days.
A week after leaving, my bank statement showed the full five-night stay taken out two times, plus a mystery amount I never agreed to. Theo at reception was lovely during the stay, though.

Our two-night stopover was pleasant overall, though the internet was painfully slow. Streaming a film in the evening was impossible and even loading email took several minutes. Parking was easy and well lit, which we appreciated.

Just one night downtown with the kids, but what a treat! The valet was so friendly, and Tobias even remembered our daughter's name and found her stuffed rabbit in the car the next morning. There was no noise at night, so everyone actually slept, and no surprise charge on the card when we left. The kids loved the pool before dinner too!

Stayed one night for a weekend away. I have been here twice before, years apart, and the manager remembered us by name at the door. Desmond asked about our previous visit, had a note left in the room, and arranged a late checkout without us asking. No wait at check-in, not a single bug in the bed, and no surprise charge on the card, which is more than I can say for some hotels in this price range. Staff throughout were attentive and professional. Small things, handled well, with no fuss.
Three nights, same result each time. The bed sagged in the middle and I woke up with a sore back before every meeting.

I had an early flight and only had time for a quick meal downstairs. Unfortunately the breakfast buffet was cold, including the eggs and the coffee urn. A little more attention to the warming trays would make a real difference for travelers like me.

Honestly this was the perfect spot for our trip! We walked to the museum, the river park and a great little ice cream shop, and the kids never once complained about their feet. In the room, the bed was not too soft or too hard and there was not a single bug in the bed, which my nervous husband checked twice. Everything was right there!

Worst sleep of my LIFE! The thing they call a sleeping surface had a crater in the middle and coils poking up through the top, I could feel every one in my ribs. Woke up both mornings with my spine screaming and a numb arm. The head cushions were thin as a folded napkin. TWO NIGHTS of this!!! The gym was decent, I'll give them that, but I was too sore to use it.

One night, early flight, and the morning food was INEDIBLE! Scrambled dishes were stiff and room temperature, the muffins were like rocks from yesterday, and the cup from the dispenser tasted like pond water left out overnight! For what this place costs per night I expected something hot!
Arrived Friday afternoon to a line out the door and waited nearly an hour for our keys.

So my husband had a work thing near the airport and the kids and I tagged along for two nights. Lovely staff, but whoever picked those sleeping surfaces needs to try one! There was a deep dip in the middle so we both rolled into it all night, and you could feel coils poking through at the edges. The head cushions were flat as crepes and my neck has been stiff since. The kids thought it was a trampoline. The pool was a hit with them, at least, warm and not crowded.

Ideal for a one-night layover with an early departure. Easy shuttle to the terminal every twenty minutes, breakfast was never cold even at 5am, and not a stain anywhere in the room. I was at my gate with time to spare.
By night two all four of us had itchy welts, and we found bugs along the bed seams. Shame, the kids adored the pool.

When I come in room, I find many long strands in the sink and on the floor, old food boxes and empty bottles from person before me, and yellow marks on the tub and pillow cover. I ask housekeeping to fix it but nobody come for four days.

We drove down for a quick overnight to see my sister's new place by the water. There was only one plug in the room, behind the dresser, so my husband and I took turns trying to charge our phones and the camera battery half the night. Parking was easy at least.

We stay in this hotel two years ago and the manager remembered us from that time. Ingrid say hello like old friends and give us room with high floor like we like. Five nights, not a single bug in the bed, and the bed was not too soft or too hard. Everybody very kind, always help with directions and taxi. Thank you so much.

Absolutely unacceptable. The bed in room 412 had springs poking through the fabric, I could feel every single coil through the sheet! My wife ended up sleeping on the armchair the second night because the mattress also dipped badly toward the wall. We asked for a topper and got a thin folded blanket. For a hotel whose whole job is getting travelers some rest, sleep should be the ONE thing you get right!! Only bright spot was Priya at the desk, who apologized and tried her best.

Our client dinner was in TWO HOURS and every place in town was booked, but the concierge found us a table within twenty minutes! Lucas saved my whole week, seriously. Give that man a raise!! And after some hotels I have suffered through, not a single bug in the bed and not a stain anywhere. FINALLY a place that gets it!

Flew in late Tuesday for a single meeting, forgot my presentation clicker at home and my tie was a wrinkled mess. The front desk was wonderful about it, Camille tracked down a steamer and lent me a clicker from the events office. No wait at check-in even at midnight, no surprise charge on the card for the clicker, and I squeezed in a 6am workout too.

The morning meal that came with our room was a JOKE! Both days the scrambled stuff in the trays had a skin on top and tasted like it had been sitting out since dawn. The bread was so stale it cracked like a cracker. My mug from the carafe was room temperature and I drank it in two gulps just to get it over with. My husband asked for something fresh and they just shrugged!! We were there at 8, not at closing. Nobody should start a vacation like this!

Five-night business stay. On the final folio there was a nightly resort fee I was never told about at booking or at the desk. That charge added up over the week and none of it was disclosed. Please itemize these upfront.

We enjoyed most of our four nights, but the room was freezing after sunset. The thermostat would not go above sixty-two and the heater only blew cold air. Maintenance came once without success. At this nightly rate we expected the heating to work.

We were here four nights for my cousin's wedding weekend, and I'll say the breakfast was a letdown. The pancakes came out cold twice, the syrup was cold too, and the sausage tasted reheated from the day before. Rosa at the omelet station was a sweetheart though and made my son a fresh one.
There's a minibar charge for items I never touched on my statement! Otherwise the kids had a blast in the pool.

We flew in for my nephew's graduation, three nights, and got to the hotel around four thinking we'd freshen up before dinner. Instead we stood in a queue for forty minutes, then were told housekeeping hadn't finished our room. We sat on lobby chairs for an hour and nearly missed the reservation.

One night before an early departure. Room heat did not work. Thermostat read 68 but the vent pushed out cold air no matter the setting. Called down at 11pm, told someone would come, nobody did. Used the spare blanket from the closet and my coat on top. Still cold all night. Slept maybe three hours. Fix the unit in that room before the next guest gets it.

Arrived at 4 PM for a 7-night stay. Room was still being serviced, and I sat in the lobby until 6:15 before getting access. No estimate given at the front counter. Parking garage was easy to find with plenty of space.

Overnight before a vacation flight, and the location could not be more practical. Easy shuttle to the terminal at 5am, ten minutes door to door. Despite the runways nearby there was no noise at night, and we could charge everything by the bed before an early start. Left the car in the lot for the week without any hassle.

I was in town two nights for a training session, so I was up early both days and down to the dining room before seven. The morning food that comes with the room sat in trays with nothing underneath keeping it hot. The scrambled stuff was congealed, the hash browns were limp, and the croissants were stale enough to crunch. I filled a mug from the big carafe and it was flat and barely above room temperature, so I bought a cup down the street on my way to the session. I did get a good swim in the pool the second evening, which helped.

About a week after my two nights at the Airport property, my bank statement showed the full amount for the stay taken out a second time, same day, same figure down to the cent, even though the folio the hotel emailed me lists only one stay and I added nothing to my room, so I would like someone to tell me where that second withdrawal came from and why my account is short by that sum.

The couple next door screamed and blasted music until 3 AM, and I heard EVERY word through the partition! Then motorcycles revved under my window at dawn. I had a client meeting that morning and got maybe two hours of sleep. The lot was tight, but I always found a spot for my car.
A week after we left, our statement showed the whole six-night stay taken out a second time. Reasonable price for the stay itself, but that duplicate needs explaining.

First night there was party next door, very loud music and people laughing until 2 in the night. I call reception two times. Second night also little noise in hallway. For this price I expect to sleep good.

I was in town four nights visiting my college roommate and planned to catch up on some freelance work in the evenings. There was no signal in the room at all on the hotel wifi, I had to sit in the lobby every night to upload anything. For what this place costs per night, the connection should just work.

For five nights the connection in our room would hold for maybe ten minutes and then vanish, so every movie we tried to stream froze into blurry squares with the spinning wheel, and my kids gave up and played cards instead. When it did work, a single photo took several minutes to send to my mom, which made the whole stay feel like we were cut off from home.

Thank you for a comfortable four-night stay. After checkout I noticed I was charged twice for the room, two identical amounts on my company card. Could someone review the second charge and contact me? The fitness room was a nice bonus between meetings.
Found bed bugs on the second night and moved rooms. Anton handled the move quickly and politely.
Week-long stay. Wifi showed no signal in the room most evenings, only worked near the elevators.

Overall a pleasant five nights, but I want to flag an issue with the nightstand. The built-in charger port was loose, so any cable I plugged in would fall out with the slightest movement. The wall socket beside it did not seem to work either. As a result I had to charge my phone at the desk across the room, which meant getting up whenever my alarm went off. A quick repair or a working outlet near the bed would make a meaningful difference for future guests.

I'm afraid we hardly slept either night. The guests next door could be heard word for word through the shared partition, someone was rolling suitcases and talking in the corridor well past midnight, and the sirens and horns from the street below came straight through the window. Earplugs did not help much.

We came up for two nights to see a musical and walk around the old market, which was lovely, and I thought $159 a night was a fair rate for the location. Then the statement came last week and there is a second withdrawal from the hotel for $74, labeled room service, dated the morning after we left. We were on the road home by then, we had stopped at my aunt's for lunch. I never ordered anything to the room.
Our anniversary fell on my work trip, and the staff made our anniversary special with flowers. The room was never cold, not a single bug in the bed. Thank you, Elena.

Two-night weekend stay. Checked my statement afterward and found I was charged twice for the second night. Same amount, posted a day apart. Please investigate the second charge and confirm in writing.

Two nights downtown with the kids and we all slept in our hoodies and socks. You could see your breath in the morning, and the dial on the wall clicked but nothing ever came out of the vents. My youngest asked if we were camping.

Work trip, three nights. The internet was painfully slow, uploads timed out and video meetings froze, so I ended up tethering most of the time. Needs an upgrade for business guests. Nadia at the desk tried resetting things for me, appreciated the effort.
Only one night, but the mattress was rock hard and the bed left me stiff for my morning meeting. I'd suggest offering a topper.
Room is nice but the radiator was cold all the night. I turn the knob many times, nothing happen. I sleep with my jacket. Night staff Pavel bring me a small heater at midnight, he was very kind.
Two nights for a supplier visit, and on the second I woke to bed bugs crawling on the pillow, so I packed and left.
The charger port was loose and NOTHING would charge overnight! Three days with a dead phone and laptop. Decent value otherwise.

We stay four nights in Downtown for holiday. Second morning I woke up with bites on my arms and neck, many small red spots in a line. I check the bed and see small brown bugs near the headboard. I show to the reception and they move us to other room on another floor, but I could not sleep good after this. We wash all our clothes in a laundry in the city. Price was not cheap, I expect more for this.
