I sleep only one night and I cannot sleep. People in next room talk and laugh until 3 in the morning, I hear every word like they are in my room. Also doors bang in the corridor all night. I have meeting next day and I am very tired. The lady at reception, Marisol, was very kind and helpful.

Third night I wake up and my arm have small red marks in a row, three and three. I look on the corner of the sleeping place and see little brown insects, like apple seeds, and black dots on the seams. I ask for new room and they move me. The pool was nice for the children.

I'm sorry to report that after one night I woke with a cluster of small red bumps along my shoulder. Looking at the corner seams of the linens, I found tiny dark spots and a small reddish-brown insect. I asked to change rooms and inspected my luggage carefully before leaving.
We very much enjoyed the amazing view from the balcony each morning. The wifi never dropped, and we could charge everything by the bed. A real pleasure.

Three nights downtown with the kids and not one spot near the nightstands to power anything up. The only wall receptacle by the beds was dead, so we had a pile of tablets and handsets lined up on the bathroom counter every night. My son's game died halfway through day two.
Ten minutes from the terminal and near our client site, a perfect spot for our trip. No noise at night, no surprise charge on the card.
Room very cold and heater would not turn on all night. I sleep in my coat. Parking was easy at least.

We drove down for my sister's birthday weekend, just two nights, and had big plans for the boardwalk, but the room was like a walk-in fridge. The dial on the wall did absolutely nothing no matter which way we turned it, the vent kept blowing air that felt like it came off an ice cube, and I slept in my hoodie and wool socks with the comforter pulled over my head. My sister wore her jacket to brush her teeth. Parking was easy at least, right by the entrance.

Three mornings in a row the food came out stone-chilled! The scrambled stuff was rubbery and the bread rolls were rock solid from yesterday. My cup from the urn tasted like it had been brewed hours ago and had zero steam. Who serves people like this?!

Our room stayed quite cold for most of the stay, as the thermostat did not seem to respond to any setting. We had to ask for extra blankets on the second night, which helped somewhat. For the rate we paid over five nights, I would have expected the heating to work.
Arrived at six and waited nearly forty minutes, as there was only one person at the front desk. Parking was straightforward.

ONE night. One. And my statement shows two separate payments to Wrenhollow Beachfront for the exact same amount on the same day! I paid at departure and got a receipt, so where did the second one come from?? Nobody gives me an answer. The room rate itself was fair, which makes this even more annoying.
The eggs were cold and the toast was stale, BOTH mornings! Ridiculous. Parking was fine, I guess.
Lovely stay overall, but the mattress was rock hard and the bed left my back sore. Not what I would expect at this price.

We came for a full five nights of sun and seafood, my husband and I, our first trip without the kids in ages, and every single morning I woke up stiff from my neck down to my hips. The middle of the sleeping surface sank into a trough, so we both rolled toward the center all night, and the cushions under our heads were as flat as folded dish rags. By day three I was stretching on the floor before we even walked to the boardwalk.

The sleeping surface in room 412 had a deep trough down the middle, so every time I turned over I slid into the dip and woke with a stiff neck and an aching spine, and the head cushions were so flat I folded them in half and stacked them just to get some lift. Parking in the covered garage was easy and close to the elevator, which was the one convenient thing about the trip.

The room was dusty everywhere! Thick grey layer on the nightstand, the TV, the window sill, even the lampshades. I wiped it down myself with a washcloth and it came away BLACK. How hard is it to dust a room?? The pool was nice, but that does not make up for this.

We loved being steps from the sand, and the kids had a blast, but the bed in our room had springs poking through on one side. My husband and I kept swapping who got the bad half! Please check those mattresses. Parking was super easy with our minivan, which was a nice surprise.

I flew in Tuesday night for a three-day training session, picked up my rental, and got to the room close to eleven, only to find the bathroom was not cleaned from whoever had it before me. There was hair in the sink, a wet towel on the floor, and a ring around the tub. I was too tired to argue so I wiped what I could with tissue and brought it up at the desk in the morning. Housekeeping fixed it that day. The lot was well lit and parking was no trouble.

The wifi was USELESS. The login page kept looping back to the start every time I entered my room number and last name. Tried it on two devices, same thing. Called the desk and was told to restart. I did. Five times! One night and I never got online once.
After a long day at the museums, no outlet by the bed meant leaving my phone to charge across the room. Nice pool though.

We were only in town one night for my cousin's wedding, so the morning meal was supposed to be our quick fuel before the ceremony. The scrambled stuff had a rubbery skin, the sausages tasted straight from the fridge, and the pot of brew had clearly been sitting since dawn. Mateo at the omelet station was lovely though.

We stay three nights at Beachfront. After we go home, I look at my bank and the hotel take the money for the room two times. Same number, same day. I call and nobody explain me why. Parking was easy, a spot near the door every day.

The valet was so friendly when I pulled in late after a long day of meetings. Desmond, if I remember his name right, offered to carry my bags and pointed me to a quiet corner of the lobby. Upstairs there was no noise at night, and the bed was not too soft or too hard. Small things, but they made a short overnight much easier.

Stayed one night for a regional sales meeting held at the hotel. The property is right on the beach, so I walked on the sand before my first session and found dinner a few blocks away. Not a single bug in the bed, and we could charge everything by the bed, laptops and phones for the whole team. Convenient for work and a short break.

Four nights for work and every night the radiator was cold. I turn the knob many times but nothing happen. Outside is windy by the sea and room become very cold. Technician come one time but not fix. I need good sleep for my work.

Three nights and the bed sagged in the middle like a hammock! I had important meetings and woke up every morning with my back aching. I asked to switch and was told they were full. Unacceptable for a business hotel! The garage was at least easy to get in and out of.

One night, arrived 11pm. On entry I found long strands in the sink and tub drain, a crumpled used washcloth on the floor, a brownish ring on the toilet seat, a dried spill on the carpet by the nightstand, and an empty food container and soda cans in the wastebasket from the previous occupant. Wiped surfaces down myself before using anything. Requested housekeeping and was told nobody was available overnight.

I come for work three nights. When I open the door, I find used cups on the table and food wrapper under the chair. In the tub drain is long black strands from other person and the sink have toothpaste spit dry on it. The floor in toilet room is sticky and smell. I ask housekeeping and they come only next day. Parking garage is close and easy, this was ok.

We spent five nights downtown for my cousin's wedding, lots of running around between the rehearsal dinner, the ceremony and a brunch on Sunday, so I did not look at my statement until a week after we got home. That is when I noticed an extra charge on my card from the hotel, a second room night that matched the first one to the cent. I called and was passed around to three people before someone said they would look into it. Still waiting to hear back. The rooftop pool was a nice break between events.

My room face the coast road, and there was traffic noise all night, motorcycles and trucks. Window is thin and I hear everything. Five nights like this is very tiring for work. Next time please give me room on the sea side. Marisol at reception was very helpful with my printing.

We walked in and there was trash from the last guest in the bin and under the desk! Takeout bags, an empty bottle, used tissues. DISGUSTING. We should not have to call down for someone to clean a room we just checked into. Ahmed from housekeeping came right up and apologized, he was great.
Had two days of video calls lined up and the internet was painfully slow, frozen every few minutes. Pricey place for that.

Housekeeping went above and beyond during my three-night stay; Rosa noticed my work shirts were wrinkled and left a steamer with a kind note. No noise at night, not a single bug in the bed, and worth every bit of the rate.

We had four nights with the kids and every single one of us slept in sweatshirts. The vent kept blowing frosty air even when we turned the dial all the way up, and my youngest said she could see her breath like a dragon. Cute, but not what you want on vacation!

In town for one night to see a show with my partner, and I needed to send a few work files before we headed out, but the wifi kept dropping every couple of minutes. Each time I had to reconnect and start the upload over. Ended up missing the start of the show.

We had a four-night layover situation on the way home from visiting my parents overseas, and honestly the location saved us. There is an easy shuttle to the terminal every twenty minutes, plus shops and a park within walking distance for the kids to stretch their legs. The bed was not too soft or too hard, not a stain anywhere on the sheets, could not have asked for better.
We arrived at four but our room was not ready until nearly six. The garage was convenient.

Breakfast in morning was not good. Cold coffee, the eggs also not warm, bread was hard like from yesterday. I have only fifteen minutes before shuttle so I cannot wait for new. The gym is small but have good machines, I use it night before.
Four nights and the pillows were flat, the bed was miserable! Paid for parking too. Fix this!

Our team come here for two days of conference near the harbor. Hotel is perfect spot for our trip, the meeting hall is five minutes walk and restaurants are all around. No wait at check-in for six people, and the wifi never dropped when we prepare slides in evening. Also nice to see the ocean at night.
Towels smelled of mildew on arrival and again after the first change. Room otherwise acceptable.

Two nights I stay and two nights I sleep maybe four hours. Room next door has TV very high volume and somebody shout. Also airplane sound every few minutes very strong, the windows shake. I ask for earplugs and it still not help. Thank you to Tomas at front, he always smile and help with bags.

The hotel's location was ideal for a week of exploring. It was walking distance to everything we wanted to see, from the museums to the old market and the riverfront, and we never once needed a taxi. In the evenings the room was never cold, and there was not a stain anywhere. I would recommend it to anyone who likes to explore on foot.
Easy shuttle to the terminal, quick ride, on time all three mornings. No noise at night, no surprise charge on the card. Driver Elias was courteous.

We came down for my cousin's wedding, four nights, and on the second morning I had a trail of red bumps across my ankle and found little black dots and a tiny flat brown thing crawling on the fitted cover. We moved to my aunt's rental for the rest of the trip.
Landed after an overnight flight and arrived at noon, only to be told my room was not ready and would not be until three. I spent the afternoon working from a lobby chair before a client dinner.

My wife and I had an early flight out after a cousin's wedding, so we booked four nights here thinking it would be restful. It was not. The couple next door argued and played music past one each night, and we could hear every word as if they were in our room. Around five the shuttle buses started idling and honking under our window, and groups kept dragging rolling bags and chatting in the corridor at all hours. We got maybe four hours a night. The parking lot was convenient and well lit, which was the one easy part.
Kids loved the waffles, but cold coffee two mornings in a row was rough for us parents. Good rate though!

Flew in late for a one-day client visit, grabbed the shuttle, and figured one night at the Airport location would be easy. It was not. The thin walls meant I heard the couple next door arguing about their luggage until well past midnight, then someone's alarm went off at 4:30 and nobody shut it off for ten minutes. I had a presentation at nine and spent most of the night staring at the ceiling. The room itself was fine, but sleep is the whole point of an airport hotel.

Arrived at 4 pm, an hour after the posted arrival time. Stood in a queue of fifteen people for 45 minutes, then was told the room still needed to be made up. Sat in the lobby another hour before going upstairs. Valet parking was quick.

We brought the kids for five nights and the room was freezing the whole time! The heater would not turn on no matter what button we pressed, and maintenance came twice without fixing it. The little ones slept in their jackets because it was so cold. For what we paid per night, we expected a warm room.

Found bed bugs along the mattress seam on the second night, plus bites on my arms. Front desk moved us to a different floor, but we packed up and left a day early anyway. The gym was well equipped, for what that's worth.

One night before an early flight. The sleeping surface was like lying on a plank, no give at all, and I woke up every hour with numb hips. The head cushions were lumpy too. Parking was easy and close to the entrance.

I was in town three nights for a training course, and by the second morning my lower back was done because the bed sagged in the middle like a hammock. Tried sleeping diagonally, tried the couch, nothing helped. Priya at the desk was lovely and found me an extra pillow.
Hair in the shower when we walked in. Someone ELSE'S hair! Gross, and nobody seemed to care!!
Weekend away for my sister's birthday ruined. Bugs in the bed, bites everywhere, and I had to throw out my clothes.
I sleep three nights and every morning my neck and spine hurt. The sleeping place is like a rock, no give at all. The head cushion is very thin, I fold it two times. Parking is good, many places.
Room never warmed up during my two nights because the thermostat stuck on cold and would not budge past 62. Reported it on day one and nobody came to look at it.
Okay, the spot is UNREAL!! Right on the beach, sand two steps from the patio! The room was never cold and not a single bug in the bed. PERFECT!

On arrival I found long strands in the tub drain and on the pillowcase, a brown ring around the sink, and an empty takeout bag and used cups from the previous guest in the wastebasket. The fitness room, on the other hand, was well equipped.
The wifi kept dropping EVERY twenty minutes! I had two video calls and got kicked off both. I'm here for work, this is the one thing I need from an airport hotel and it simply did not work. Fix it!

Only one outlet by the nightstand and the charger port was loose, so my phone would not charge unless I propped the cable at an angle. Woke up at 20 percent before a flight. Gym was open early, which was useful.

We cut the trip short when my husband's conference moved, called ahead, got a confirmation number, and still got billed for a night I cancelled. The charge showed up four days after we got home. The kids did enjoy the pool on the nights we stayed, at least.
We arrive at 2 o'clock but room is not prepared. We wait in the lobby with bags and finally checked in after 5. Very tired from travel. Parking garage is expensive but easy to find.

I stay one night for work. The connection in the room not work good, every five minutes it go away and come again. I can not send my report to my office. But the lady Priya at reception was very kind with me.

My husband had to finish some work during our trip and the connection kept cutting out every few minutes, so his uploads never finished and the kids' cartoons froze constantly. Not fun! But Desmond at the front counter was a sweetheart and even gave the kids stickers.

During my five nights the wireless connection in my room was unreliable. Web pages took a minute or more to open, and my evening shows froze and buffered every few minutes. A couple of times a day it disconnected entirely and I had to reconnect. I hoped to get some light work done online and mostly could not.

Second night I see small bed bugs on the pillow and my legs have red bites. We ask to move and they give new room but I cannot sleep after this. Pool is nice but I don't enjoy because I worry all the time.
Fun trip with the kids, but there's a charge still pending two weeks later! Rate was fair otherwise.
Came down for a sales meeting, stayed right on the beach, walked the shoreline before calls, breakfast was never cold, and no noise at night either.
Towels smelled musty, like they were never fully dried. Pool area looked nice though.

After checkout I see a minibar charge for items I never touched. I did not even open the minibar in five nights. I send email two times and still no answer. The room price is already high, so this is more frustrating.
We waited an hour to check in on Saturday afternoon. Once it was our turn, Devon was gracious and apologetic.
Two nights and almost no sleep. The people next door shouted and played music until 3am, and every footstep and conversation in the corridor came right through. Earplugs did nothing.

We drove down for a long weekend at the beach, our first trip since the baby, and were excited that breakfast was included. All three mornings the eggs were cold and rubbery, the toast was stale, and the coffee urn was lukewarm by eight. My partner tried going down right when it opened and it was no better, so it seems the food sits out a long time before anyone eats it. Given the nightly rate, we expected a hot plate in the morning.

We rolled in at 3pm sharp and stood in the lobby for TWO HOURS while they told us our room was still being turned over! Two hours with our suitcases and a cranky kid! Housekeeping was still vacuuming when we finally got upstairs. Ridiculous. At least the garage across the street had plenty of open spaces.
Line out the door at check-in, close to an hour. Decent rate for the area though.

Walked into the bathroom on the first night and found hair in the shower, on the soap dish, and stuck to the drain cover. The sink had a ring of toothpaste and there was a smear on the mirror. I wiped what I could with tissues and asked for housekeeping the next morning, and the room was better after that, but a first impression like this makes you wonder about everything else. Valet parking was quick and the attendants were careful with the car.

I check out on Thursday and two days later there is an extra charge on my card from the hotel. Nobody explain what is it. I write to the front desk and still no reply. Parking was included and this was fine.
Lovely beach weekend, but we got a minibar charge for items I never touched! Parking was easy.
The thin walls made it hard to sleep when neighbors came in late. Ana at the front desk was very kind.

Oh boy, where to start. We came in from a day of sightseeing with two little ones and the room felt like the inside of a fridge. The dial on the wall unit did nothing no matter which way I turned it, and the vent just pushed out icy air. My son slept in his hoodie and hat, and I could see my breath when I got up in the night. We piled every spare comforter from the closet on the kids. The pool was lovely though, and the kids loved the little slide.
I found bed bugs on my second night and had to throw out my clothes before flying home.

So I was in for a two-night trade show, flew in late after a delayed connection, and reached the hotel near midnight. Around four in the morning I woke up scratching and found a trail of small red bumps marching up my forearm, three or four in a neat row. I flipped on the lamp, pulled the linens away, and there were tiny dark specks along the seams and one flat brownish thing the size of an apple seed crawling near the headboard. I bagged my suitcase, moved to another floor, and spent the show worrying I'd carried them home.

So we did six nights downtown for my sister's wedding and the rehearsal dinner and then a couple of days of museums after. Every night I'd go to power up my cell before sleep and there was nowhere near the nightstand to hook the cord into. The one spot behind the lamp was dead, and I tried it with three different cords. I ended up leaving my mobile on the counter across the room overnight, which meant no alarm by my head, and my work computer died midway through a meeting on day four because the only live spot was taken by the kettle.
No wait at check-in, no surprise charge on the card, and housekeeping went above and beyond all week, even leaving a good-luck note from Rosa.

We arrive late after long flight and the room is not good. In the sink there are many little black curls from someone shaving. Under the sofa I find old food wrapper and empty bottle. The cover on the sleeping place have yellow mark and the floor feel sticky under my feet. Also the tub have pink ring around. For this money, 180 per night, I expect much better.

We have stayed here a few times over the years, and the manager remembered us by name and asked about our son's swim team. It is a small thing, but it made the stay feel personal. The bed was not too soft or too hard, and there was no surprise charge on the card at checkout. A gracious team all around.

My flight landed at noon and I arrived around one, hoping to rest before an evening dinner with a client. I was told the room was still being prepared and was asked to come back in an hour, then another hour after that. I finally checked in after 5, which left me barely enough time to change. I understand that turnover takes time, but some estimate up front would have helped me plan. The fitness room was well kept and I used it the next morning.

I come for two days of work meetings and arrive at 3 o'clock, the normal check-in time. The room was not ready and the lady at desk say maybe thirty minutes. It become two hours. I sit in the lobby with my laptop and suitcase and I cannot prepare for the meeting good. Nobody come to tell me update, I must ask again and again. The gym is small but okay, I use it one morning.

The room was comfortable, but the thin walls let through every television and conversation from the rooms on either side. Earplugs at the front desk, or better insulation, would make a real difference for guests staying more than one night.

We arrived at the Beachfront property around four in the afternoon, an hour after the stated arrival time, and were told our room was still being prepared. We sat in the lobby with our luggage for nearly two and a half hours, asking politely for an update more than once. By the time we were given access it was dark and we had missed the sunset we had driven six hours to see. I understand delays happen, but a realistic estimate at the front counter would have helped.

The hotel is in very good place. It is walking distance to everything, museums, restaurants, the old market, the river park. We leave the car three days and walk every day, it was very nice for us. In the evening we walk to hotel easy and safe. Also no wait at check-in, the bed was not too soft or too hard, and no surprise charge on the card when we leave. This hotel is good for people who want to see the city by foot.

The mattress had springs poking through on one side, so I slept on the edge of the bed for all three nights. A replacement would help guests who travel often for work. The covered parking was convenient.

On our second morning my husband had a row of red bumps across his shoulder, and I found tiny rust-colored dots and a flat brown crawling thing on the pillowcase seam, so we packed up and left that afternoon.
Construction started at 7 right outside the window. Not great, even at a low nightly rate.

I want to be fair, as the staff were courteous, but our single night was uncomfortable. The room never rose above what felt like the low sixties despite the control panel being set much higher, and the vent seemed to be pushing in outside air. We wore sweaters and socks to sleep and still woke up shivering around three. Maintenance came up and tapped at the unit but could not get it going. It was a shame for a beach stay.

For business trip this hotel is very good position. Easy shuttle to the terminal, every twenty minutes, and the ride is only five minutes. I have early flight on last day and I don't worry. There are some offices and places to eat nearby, so I walk to my meetings two days. Also no wait at check-in, the wifi never dropped when I work in room, and breakfast was never cold. For travel with work I think this is the best choice near airport.
